top.headline: How Trump's push to prosecute noncitizen voters produced almost nothing
top.blurb: ProPublica found that after the administration diverted Homeland Security Investigations — normally focused on trafficking and smuggling — toward hunting noncitizen voters, a Justice Department analysis showed fewer than 150 people were referred for prosecution and just 41 charged between January 2025 and May 2026, with agents repeatedly finding database matches that didn't hold up.

top.headline: Voters are fed up with data centers. Both parties are racing to cash in on it
top.blurb: A bipartisan backlash against AI data centers — over electricity bills and local strain — has become a live midterm issue, with campaigns and outside groups pouring more than $45 million into ads mentioning them this year, almost all of it hostile. Republicans, caught between Trump's build-out push and angry voters, look the most exposed.

top.headline: Republicans are souring on the economy fast
top.blurb: Republican confidence in the economy has fallen 15 points since February, from 97.1 to 82 on the University of Michigan's index — a drop usually seen only in the party out of power. It's an ominous signal for Trump heading into the final two months before the midterms.

top.headline: Odisha redrew a wildlife sanctuary's map to open it up for bauxite mining
top.blurb: A two-part investigation found Odisha, with help from India's top wildlife body, redrew Karlapat Wildlife Sanctuary's boundaries to carve out bauxite blocks, then helped Vedanta split a single mining project in two to dodge stricter forest-clearance rules. Forest inside an elephant corridor is now set to be handed over for mining.

top.headline: The US and Iran are now trading tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz
top.blurb: Washington and Tehran escalated their tit-for-tat campaign over the past day: the US struck three Iranian oil tankers, and Iran's Revolutionary Guard hit back at three tankers and three US-linked vessels near the strait, plus a ballistic missile fired toward a US carrier group. No ships were hit.

top.headline: Yemeni forces claim a strategic district as Houthi clashes intensify
top.blurb: Yemen's army says it recaptured Hais district, linking Hodeidah, Taiz and Ibb provinces, amid fighting that has killed more than 120 people since Thursday by AFP's tally and displaced nearly 1,800 families in two days — the worst violence since a ceasefire collapsed in July.

top.headline: Witkoff and Kushner hold 'substantive' Kyiv talks after meeting Putin in Moscow
top.blurb: Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Sunday, their first visit to Ukraine, a day after more than three hours of talks with Putin in Moscow. Both sides called the discussions productive, though neither offered specifics on what, if anything, had been agreed.

top.headline: Ishan Kishan smashes an unbeaten century on the Duleep Trophy final's opening day
top.blurb: East Zone captain Ishan Kishan reached his century off 122 balls and finished day one unbeaten on 111, as East Zone closed on 385 for 4 against South Zone in Chennai. Kishan also passed 4,000 first-class runs during the innings, pushing his case for a Test recall.

top.headline: South Africa thump Zimbabwe to win the Namibia T20I Tri-Series
top.blurb: South Africa posted 205 for 5 in Windhoek and bowled Zimbabwe out for 157 to win the final by 48 runs, taking the tri-series title despite missing injured openers Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Andile Simelane.

top.headline: Kennedy Center removes a landmark Joel Shapiro sculpture without warning
top.blurb: Workers disassembled 'Blue,' Joel Shapiro's towering stick-figure sculpture installed on the Kennedy Center's grounds since 2019, with no advance notice; the center called it routine deinstallation of donated art. A former curator says it was targeted after Trump's takeover of the institution. Shapiro died in 2025.

bengal.headline: Landslide-formed natural dam on the Teesta raises fresh flood fears in North Bengal
bengal.blurb: A landslide near Mirik dammed the Rangbhang Khola and another blocked the Teesta near its confluence with the Chyakoong, leaving Darjeeling, Kalimpong and Jalpaiguri residents downstream bracing for flash floods if either gives way.

travel.headline: Lonely Planet's 23 best places to travel this fall
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet's fall picks run from Seoul to the Seychelles, with a nod to Canada's Prince Edward Island for gentle cycling once summer crowds thin and temperatures settle near 20°C.

travel.headline: 36 years of watching songbirds pass through one small Maine island
travel.blurb: Ahead of a September 9 Cornell lecture, ornithologist Sara Morris previews decades of dawn fieldwork banding warblers and orioles at a long-running research station on Appledore Island, Maine, and how the migration she tracks is shifting.

happy.headline: Queen Camilla reunited Winnie-the-Pooh with a friend he'd been missing for 90 years
happy.blurb: The real stuffed animals behind A.A. Milne's stories live at the New York Public Library, minus Roo, lost since the 1930s. On a state visit, Queen Camilla presented a replica by Merrythought, the firm that made the originals in the 1920s, completing the set before the books' 100th anniversary.

tech_top.headline: OpenAI says its new GPT-6 Astra model may represent AGI
tech_top.blurb: OpenAI president Greg Brockman called GPT-6 Astra a 'generational leap' that could eventually be seen as the arrival of artificial general intelligence. It's also the first model OpenAI has classified as reaching a 'critical' cybersecurity threshold — able to find and exploit unknown vulnerabilities without step-by-step human guidance.
tech_top.pm_note: A vendor calling its own model AGI-adjacent is a marketing claim as much as a technical one — read the safety classification, not the press line, before planning a roadmap around it.

tech_top.headline: US and China to discuss AI-directed cyberattacks at September 24 talks
tech_top.blurb: Ahead of a planned Trump-Xi summit, sources say the US will push a proposal for American and Chinese AI labs to share information and self-regulate against AI-directed cyberattacks, while China is expected to revisit US chip export controls.
tech_top.pm_note: Two rival AI ecosystems discussing shared defenses against AI-directed attacks is a tacit admission that neither can secure this alone — worth watching if your stack touches either country's models.

tech_top.headline: All 20 G20 nations endorse a light-touch US framework for AI regulation
tech_top.blurb: The non-binding 'Carolina Principles,' endorsed unanimously including by China and Russia, urge sector-specific rules over new regulators and close coordination with industry, reserving new regulation for genuinely novel risks rather than every new AI capability.
tech_top.pm_note: A global consensus for light-touch rules lowers the near-term compliance bar everywhere at once — useful now, but today's product decisions may need retrofitting once any one bloc breaks ranks.

tech_more.headline: Nvidia launches a free tool to pool home AI compute across a network
tech_more.blurb: Nvidia's Personal AI Router, in beta, distributes local AI inference workloads across compatible computers on the same network rather than routing them to the cloud.

tech_101.text: A hypothetical AI that matches or exceeds human ability across essentially any intellectual task, rather than excelling narrowly. No model has been independently verified to reach it, so a company's own AGI claim is a marketing and morale signal as much as a technical benchmark.

Government restrictions on selling sensitive technology, like advanced AI chips, to specific countries — the US's main lever for slowing a rival's AI progress. China raising them at AI-safety talks signals it still sees the restrictions, not shared safety norms, as the real agenda.

science.headline: New material changes color invisibly, opening a path to unforgeable security tags
science.blurb: Researchers created davyne, a mineral-inspired material that shifts color only in near-infrared light, invisible to the naked eye and detectable solely with a spectrometer or infrared camera. Unlike related color-changing minerals, it stays white under ordinary light, making it a candidate for anti-counterfeiting tags nobody can see, let alone copy.

science.headline: Astronomers directly detect the faint signal of hydrogen from billions of years ago
science.blurb: South Africa's MeerKAT telescope directly detected the faint 21-centimetre radio signal of neutral hydrogen gas at distances of 3.67 and 4.76 billion light-years, a technique astronomers hope will eventually map how galaxies formed and dark matter shaped the early universe.

science.headline: A five-metal catalyst breaks down a greenhouse gas that lingers 50,000 years
science.blurb: An entropy-stabilized aluminate catalyst made from five metals improved decomposition of CF4, a semiconductor-industry greenhouse gas that can persist in the atmosphere for tens of thousands of years, by 2.3-fold over a standard alumina catalyst.

philosophy.headline: In Zen, asking whether you have free will is the wrong question
philosophy.blurb: The free will versus determinism debate assumes a fixed 'I' who either chooses freely or doesn't, this essay argues — but Zen, echoing Jung's account of the ego as a mere complex of the unconscious, questions whether that self exists at all. If there's no one to be pushed around, the question dissolves rather than resolves.

philosophy.headline: AI companies are hiring philosophers, and philosophy graduates are noticing
philosophy.blurb: US philosophy graduates had a lower 2024 unemployment rate than computer science graduates, as AI firms recruit for expertise in ethics, reasoning and safety. As AI spreads through healthcare, law and defence, questions of fairness and accountability are pulling philosophers straight out of academia.

philosophy_101.text: For Jung, the ego isn't a fixed inner ruler but one complex among many in the unconscious — a useful but partial construct. It's the idea this week's Zen essay leans on to argue there may be no fixed 'self' to have or lack free will in the first place.

The work of making an AI system's goals and behavior match human intentions and values, rather than just its stated instructions. It draws directly on ethics and philosophy of mind — one reason philosophy graduates are increasingly hired into AI labs.
